title: Robust enhanced index tracking portfolio selection under distributional uncertainty
data_sources: Yahoo! Finance monthly adjusted closing prices Jan 2015 - Dec 2024 for tickers AAPL, NVDA, MSFT, AVGO, ORCL, JNJ, ABBV, LLY, UNH, ABT, BRK-B, JPM, V, BAC, MA, AMZN, TSLA, HD, MCD, BKNG, WMT, COST, KO, PG, PM and benchmark index (not named, S&P500 implied) - file not named, download via Yahoo! Finance
sample: Monthly loss data for 25 US stocks (5 largest by market cap per sector: Technology, Healthcare, Financial Services, Consumer Cyclical, Consumer Defensive; tickers AAPL, NVDA, MSFT, AVGO, ORCL, JNJ, ABBV, LLY, UNH, ABT, BRK-B, JPM, V, BAC, MA, AMZN, TSLA, HD, MCD, BKNG, WMT, COST, KO, PG, PM) from Yahoo! Finance. Loss x_{i,t}= -(P_{i,t+1}-P_{i,t})/P_{i,t} where P_{i,t} is adjusted closing price. Vector x_t=(x_{1,t},...,x_{25,t}). No additional filters stated. Sample sizes: count_TotalStocks_25=25 total, count_Technology_5 etc each 5, count_InSampleMonths_60=60 in-sample (2015-2019) rolling, count_OutSampleMonths_60=60 out-of-sample (2020-2024), count_TotalMonths_120=120
method: Step 1: Universe construction. Fix n=25. For each of 5 sectors collect 5 largest companies by market capitalization as listed in sample.
Step 2: Data download. Retrieve monthly adjusted closing prices P_{i,t} from Yahoo! Finance for Jan 2015 - Dec 2024.
Step 3: Return definition. Compute monthly loss rate x_{i,t}= -(P_{i,t+1}-P_{i,t})/P_{i,t}; return is -x_{i,t}. Form vector x_t.

Step 4: Uncertainty set M_{n+1}(mu,Sigma) specification. Estimate mu and Sigma as sample mean vector and sample covariance matrix from current 60-month in-sample window. Define M set as all distributions G,F with same mean mu and covariance Sigma positive definite.

Step 5: Uncertainty set D_{n+1}(gamma1,gamma2) specification. Compute hat mu and hat Sigma as sample mean and covariance from initial in-sample (Jan 2015-Dec 2019). For gamma1,gamma2 calibration, use rolling 60-month windows i, compute gamma1i=(hat mu_{n,i}-hat mu_n)' hat Sigma_n^{-1} (hat mu_{n,i}-hat mu_n) and gamma2i=||hat Sigma_i - hat Sigma||_F; set gamma1=average gamma1i=0.22 (0.21 in sensitivity figures) and gamma2=average gamma2i=0.025.

Step 6: Index loss X0. Use benchmark index loss X0 with mean mu0 and variance sigma0^2 included in joint mu,Sigma. Excess target defines X_alpha = X0 + alpha with alpha=-0.04 (chosen because -bar alpha=0.0075 average excess, so -alpha=0.04 > -bar alpha).

Step 7: Model parameters. Set r0=0.02 (chosen bar r=0.0176 < r0 < -alpha) for M set; r=-0.01 (<r0) for D set; kappa=5 (kappa>kappa0=4.65 where kappa0=[2+2 sqrt(b0+1)]/b0) for main results. Weight constraints: allow short selling W=R^n or prohibit W=A^n=[0,inf)^n with omega'e=1.

Step 8: Closed-form solutions under M set (Sec 3). Compute constants alpha*=alpha+mu0, u=(e'Sigma_n^{-1} e)(mu_n'Sigma_n^{-1} mu_n)-(e'Sigma_n^{-1} mu_n)^2, c0=e'Sigma_n^{-1} e, c1=e'Sigma_n^{-1} mu_n, c2=mu_n'Sigma_n^{-1} mu_n, c3=b'Sigma_n^{-1} mu_n, c4=b'Sigma_n^{-1} e, c5=b'Sigma_n^{-1} b, b0=c0/u, b1=c1/u, b2=c2/u. For m=1 use Theorem 1(i) formula for omega_{1,kappa}^* with s_{1,kappa} as printed; for m=2 use Theorem 1(ii) formula with s_{2,kappa}. For ER/TSV-only use Proposition 1 formulas. For M-V and V use MV-model-1 and V-model-1 closed forms as printed.

Step 9: Convex optimization under D set (Sec 4). Solve second-order cone programs: Thm 2 (m=1) problem ob-m=1, Thm 2 (m=2) ob-m=2, Prop 2 (ER) ob-m=1-only/ob-m=2-only, Prop 3 (M-V/V) ob-MV-D/ob-V-D with variables omega in W, s in R+, t in R+, using hat mu_n, hat mu0, hat Sigma, gamma1, gamma2, alpha* = alpha+hat mu0, a=(omega,-1). Use convex solver.

Step 10: Back-test. Initial window Jan 2015-Dec 2019 estimate parameters solve optimal omega0*. Compute out-of-sample portfolio return R1= -omega0* ' x1 for Jan 2020. Roll window forward one month (Feb 2015-Jan 2020 etc), re-estimate, re-solve, compute Rt= -omega_{t-1}* ' x_t for t=1..60 (Jan 2020-Dec 2024). Repeat for each model (a) M-ER m=1, (b) ER m=1, (c) M-TSV m=2, (d) TSV m=2, (e) M-V, (f) V, (g) EWP equal weights 1/25.

Step 11: Performance metrics. From 60 out-of-sample returns compute CW (cumulative wealth starting at 1, compounded), Mean Return (sample mean of Rt), SD (sample standard deviation), ER (expected regret = sample mean of (omega'X - X0 -alpha)_+ ), TSV (sample mean of squared excess), Sharpe, Sortino, Omega ratios as defined in cited references. Report values in Table M (M set, alpha=-0.04,r0=0.02,kappa=5) and Table D (D set, alpha=-0.04,r=-0.01,gamma1=0.22,gamma2=0.025,kappa=5) separately with/without short selling; box best per column.

Step 12: Sensitivity to kappa. Vary kappa over (kappa0,inf) for M-ER and (0,inf) for M-TSV/M-V, recompute out-of-sample CW, Sharpe, Sortino, Omega with/without short selling under both uncertainty sets; plot Figs 2-7 and record optimal/crossover kappa values as printed.
